name: Hearthglen
summary: In the northern hills of the Western Plaguelands, Hearthglen holds firm. Its walls survived Lordaeron's fall, and the Scarlet Crusade now uses the settlement and its farmlands as a northern stronghold and training ground.

sections.title: A Bastion in the Blight
sections.body:
Hearthglen still looks like a living town of Lordaeron, while nearby Andorhal lies in skeletal ruin. Its lumber mill, scout towers, stables, and working mine are still here. Lord Tirion Fordring once governed from Mardenholde Keep. During the Second War, Hearthglen prospered and stood staunchly defended.

When the Plague of Undeath swept Lordaeron during the Third War, Prince Arthas Menethil intercepted tainted grain here. He purged the infected townsfolk and joined Uther the Lightbringer to repel a massive Scourge siege. Hearthglen's formidable walls survived intact.

sections.title: Under the Scarlet Banner
sections.body:
After the kingdom's collapse, the Silver Hand fell into disarray. Tirion's son, Taelan Fordring, renounced the order and joined the Scarlet Crusade. Grief and zealotry soon consumed the fortress. Scarlet crusaders now patrol Hearthglen's approaches and man its ramparts. They execute any outsider, living or undead, who trespasses on their land.

Highlord Taelan Fordring rules from Mardenholde Keep. From there, he serves the Crusade's uncompromising war against the Plaguelands.

faq.q: Why does Hearthglen look so clean compared to the rest of the Plaguelands?
faq.answer: Prince Arthas and Uther the Lightbringer helped spare Hearthglen from utter ruin during the Third War. They slew early plague victims and broke a massive Scourge siege. Later, the Scarlet Crusade fortified the pass and valley, purging the encroaching Scourge before the rot could take hold.

aliases: who is in charge of hearthglen
faq.answer: The Scarlet Crusade controls Hearthglen from Mardenholde Keep, where Highlord Taelan Fordring rules. He is the son of Tirion Fordring, the former lord and famed paladin.

faq.q: Is Hearthglen friendly to Alliance or Horde visitors?
faq.answer: No. The Scarlet Crusade treats all outsiders with extreme hostility and paranoia. They see Horde members as monstrous abominations. Unaligned Alliance travelers are condemned as plague-carriers or heretics and marked for execution on sight.

Years before the Third War, Tirion was stripped of his title and excommunicated by the Alliance for defending an honorable orc named Eitrigg. Exiled to the wilds, he left Hearthglen behind. Command of Mardenholde eventually passed to his son, Taelan.

angles.text: As a paladin, you walk the approaches to a place once home to Tirion Fordring. His son now holds Hearthglen for the Scarlet Crusade. The town shows how tragically the order splintered into a fanatical crusade.
As a Forsaken, you face a lethal thorn in the north at Hearthglen. Its crusaders hate the undead and patrol to eradicate any scouts venturing north from Andorhal.
